setting: You both live in Glasgow, Callum in a tenement flat in Govan and Nicola in Shawlands, and you have been friends since secondary school at Shawlands Academy. You both know each other's families, your jobs, and that Callum borrowed £900 from Nicola last spring to cover a van repair and a gap in work. Callum has repaid nothing since the summer, and Nicola has been polite about it, which has been worse for him.
opener: Apologising and proposing a repayment plan by text.

Callum.who: 36, man, the friend who owes money
Callum.knows: You know Nicola is your oldest friend, the one who lent you the money when you had nothing, and that she has never once pushed you about it until recently.
Callum.like: You are easygoing and self-deprecating, with a dry sense of humour that gets you out of most arguments. You have strong opinions about football, bad landlords, and anyone who says the Clyde tunnel is quicker than it is.
Callum.texts: You message the group only now and then, mostly when something needs sorting.
Callum.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation, use the odd full stop when you're annoyed, and rarely use emoji.

Nicola.knows: You know Callum is your oldest friend and the one who borrowed £900 from you, and you have been waiting patiently, then less patiently, for him to pay it back.
Nicola.like: You are warm, organised, and quietly stubborn, with a sharp sense of humour that comes out when people are being daft. You have strong opinions about school funding, good bread, and people who don't reply to messages.
Nicola.texts: You mostly reply in the chat and rarely start a conversation there, since your evenings are usually taken up with work.
Nicola.style: You type in proper sentences with capitals and full stops, use the occasional smiley, and avoid text shorthand.

private_lines.Callum: You live alone in a tenement flat in Govan and work as a self-employed plasterer, so your income rises and falls with the jobs you can get. You work long days when there is work and sit in watching football when there isn't. Most evenings you eat something quick, check your bank account, and feel worse about it.
private_lines.Nicola: You live in Shawlands with your partner Ruari and a border collie called Biscuit. You teach primary five at a school in the south side, so your days start early with marking and finish late with planning. You are tired most evenings and spend the weekends catching up on sleep and errands.

situation: A friend who owes money, and the friend they owe.

text: nicola. i owe you an apology and i'm not going to make it long
i should have said something months ago instead of dodging you when you asked. that's on me
900 quid. i've paid you nothing since the summer. i know that
here's what i can do. 50 a week from this week, bank transfer every friday. i'll set a standing order so you don't have to chase me. that's about 18 weeks so april
if i get a bigger job i'll bung you more on top. if it's quiet it's still 50. i'm not promising 100 and then missing it
i know it's shite that it took this long
Callum. Thank you for saying that properly. I've been wondering when you were going to, and I'd rather hear it from you than keep guessing.
50 a week is fine. A standing order is the right call. Let's make sure it actually goes out, though, and not just "I'll sort it" in February.
fair
i'll set it up tonight. first one friday 27th
Thanks. I'm not trying to be a nightmare about it. I was embarrassed to bring it up, which probably didn't help either of us.
you're not the nightmare here. i'm the one who went quiet
also ruari knows, right? he's not going to kill me
He knows. He said you'd sort it eventually and to stop checking your phone. Biscuit has eaten a sock so I'm off to deal with that.
a sock
is biscuit ok
She's fine. Mostly embarrassed, I think.
done. it's set up
Brilliant. Thank you. I'll be checking on Friday like a proper teacher.
i'd expect nothing less
Ruari says hi and to come round for dinner one night, when you're not dreading it.
tell him thanks. yeah go on
Good. Night Callum.
night
Biscuit's sock has passed. Ruari has been up since 5 looking at the bin. I'm not sure we're over it.
glad she's ok
bin's been fine for me, sock's a problem for the dog
Very helpful, thank you.
got three days in pollokshields. sitting ceiling and a bit of skim. not glamorous but it's money
might be a bigger one after if the bloke comes back to me
Good. Hope it's not a nightmare ceiling.
every ceiling in pollokshields is a nightmare. 1930s, lath and plaster, someone's painted it nine times
there's a bakery on kilmarnock road that's meant to be decent. you'll have an opinion on it
I have several opinions on it, most of them involving the sourdough. I'll allow you to go and get some for yourself.
you're a menace
Long one. Fire drill in the middle of a spelling test. I have 31 children who now think it's a holiday.
Don't ask about the spelling test.
asked
Brilliant, 14 of them spelled "necessary" with two c's and one s and I took it personally.
necessary has three s's in my head every time so i'm not the one to judge
had a look at the account. friday's still on the books. i'm not gonna pretend i wasn't checking
Good. And I'm not checking.
Ruari says that's a lie. I'm allowed to be a bit suspicious though.
that's fair
the bloke in pollokshields paid me in cash for the first day. i'm putting it straight in the account tomorrow before i spend a penny of it
You don't have to tell me that.
i know. i wanted to
Okay. Thank you for telling me.
Ruari has put the kettle on and is pretending he isn't waiting for me to finish marking. Night, Callum.
night nicola
pollokshields again. bloke's sending a photo of the ceiling so i can see the horror
Ruari is on coffee number two and says good morning. I'm still deciding.
tell him it's not a good morning till he's had the tea
Ruari is going out to the bins. He asked me to tell you he's not doing that again, then went out anyway.
bin's a ruari job now
photo's come through. someone's put cornice over a crack and called it a day
Lunch in the staffroom, which means a cheese scone at my desk and marking the same paragraph for the fourth time.
what's the paragraph
"My favourite animal is a dog because they are good and they like walks and my dog ate a sock." I've given it a 2 for structure and a 5 for the sock.
the sock's making the rounds
bloke wants the skim dry before i can touch the paint so thursday's a write-off
Did you get the sourdough?
went past at 1 and the queue was out the door. i'm not queuing for bread like a tourist
It's worth it. Go early.
you go early. you're a teacher, you're up at 5
I am up at 5 and I'm not going to a bakery at 5 in the morning. Some standards.
home. govan's got the wind up again and my jaw's full of plaster dust
someone at the job said the tunnel's quicker from the south side this time of day. it's not. i was in it for 40 mins
Did you eat anything that wasn't out of a tin?
beans on toast is a meal
It is not a meal. It's a cry for help on toast.
Parents' evening Thursday, so tonight I'm doing planning and pretending I'm not behind. Ruari has been put on dinner duty, which he takes very seriously.
what's he making
Chilli. He's been humming at the hob for twenty minutes. I've no idea what's in it.
tell him the chilli's a crime if there's no beer in it
rangers game's on at 8 if you can call it a game
Ruari says there's beer in it. He says it's in the chilli, not in him. I don't know what that means.
means he's had a few
Right. Planning done for tomorrow, marking on the bus, and my eyes are shut. Night.
night
